bioMerieux (BIM-FR): a locked-in reagent franchise at a trough multiple, with its cause for concern clearing, but a modest earnings engine leaves the return resting on a re-rating

Triaging A&J Memo, 24 November 2026

#0 The investment case

The case in one line. bioMerieux is a locked-in reagent franchise trading at the 8th percentile of its ten-year multiple, and the cause of its de-rating (two weak flu seasons and three guidance cuts) is now clearing. Its earnings engine is modest, so the return depends more on the multiple than on earnings.

1. The one idea: the installed base is locked in, but the number of tests run through it is not

bioMerieux places closed diagnostic instruments in hospital laboratories and then sells the proprietary reagents that run on them. Reagents and services are 91% of sales, contracts run five to ten years, and a laboratory that leaves must revalidate its testing. bioMerieux holds over 75% of high-plex syndromic molecular testing (the BIOFIRE range) and about 40% of clinical microbiology.

The locked-in base and the variable test volume have three consequences:

  • The competitive position is strong, because customers rarely leave.
  • The main risk is test volume and price per test, above all the strength of the winter respiratory season, because respiratory panels are over 20% of sales.
  • Earnings are geared to volume: two points of volume move earnings per share by about 6%.

2. The change: three positive forces of unequal size and durability

CyclicalLargeNot durable

Respiratory testing is recovering after two weak winters. United States laboratory flu positivity was 7.6% in late October against 0.6% a year earlier, and the comparison base for the next three quarters is very low.

A lower barMedium

The company is now measured against targets it can beat. In July 2026 management rebased its 2027 to 2028 targets from 7% organic sales growth to 3% to 6%, with profit growing faster than sales.

InternalMediumDurable

Self-help and new ownership are adding pressure for returns. The GO Simple cost programme is delivering, the chief executive's term is renewed to 2030, Exor is doubling its stake to 8.5% and taking a board seat, and three launches arrive in 2027 (VITEK PRO, the SPOTFIRE vaginitis panel and the SpinChip troponin test).

The headwinds are real and mostly structural, and together they cost one to two points of growth and absorb most of the cost savings. Currency takes about EUR 35m from operating profit in 2026 and again in 2027; resin and electronics costs rise in 2027; United States payers resist large panels; China is still shrinking; and Waters now owns the other half of the microbiology duopoly. As a result, the cyclical respiratory recovery does the lifting in 2027, and the structural forces set the pace from 2028.

The earnings response is modest, so the larger movement is in the narrative, from "serial downgrader" to "reset delivered". My forecasts imply three expectations for the next events:

  • The 2026 guidance should be met near its middle at the full-year results on 26-Feb-27.
  • The 2027 guidance should start cautious and has roughly a 30% chance of being raised by July 2027.
  • Consensus EPS, which has risen 1% in three months after falling 14% in twelve, should edge up by low single digits over the next two events.
My EPS forecasts are at consensus for 2027 and 2% below consensus for 2028, so the case does not rest on forecasts above the market's.

The franchise's quality shows in dominant market shares, locked-in customers, a 56% gross margin and net cash. Its financial conversion is only average: the 17% operating margin is well short of DiaSorin's, the return on invested capital is 12%, and capital spending takes 8% to 9% of sales.

Management is rigorous and candid, but its delivery record is mixed. Sales guidance was beaten in 2023 and 2024 and cut in 2025 and 2026. Profit guidance was met or beaten in 2024 and 2025 and cut in 2026. The mid-term plan was rebased five months after the chief executive said the company was exceeding it. The controlling family holds 55% of the capital and 69% of the votes.

The foundation supports the reagent revenue stream, but it does not yet justify a premium multiple for delivery.

5. The setup: a cause for concern clearing at a trough multiple, but in a business that is not low-cyclicality

The best-fitting setup is "a cause for concern clearing in a high-quality, low-cyclicality business on a first- or second-quartile multiple, leading to reversion to normal". Four of the setup's elements are present and four are missing, and the missing four explain why the expected return is ordinary rather than exceptional.

Present

  • A first-quartile multiple: 17.9 times two-year forward earnings, the 8th percentile of ten years
  • An identifiable cause for concern: two weak respiratory seasons, three guidance cuts and the target reset
  • Evidence that the concern is clearing: third-quarter organic growth of 8.1%, guidance held, an early flu season and estimates turning up
  • A high-quality franchise

Missing

  • Low cyclicality: a fifth of sales swings with epidemiology
  • An unchanged "normal" to revert to: the growth target is permanently lower, so the old multiple is the wrong anchor
  • Momentum: the dashboard still reads sell-side momentum F and technical momentum D
  • A clean delivery record

The base case offers roughly 1.4 of upside for each 1 of downside, and the better case relies on a re-rating that I think is generous.

  • Base case (50%). If the case plays out on my forecasts and the multiple recovers to about 19.5 times, the 18-month return is about +21%.
  • Guideline multiple. At the guideline fair multiple of 23.0 times, the 18-month return is about +43%.
  • Worse case (30%). If the case fails (another mild winter, reimbursement cuts and a multiple of 15 times), the return is about (15)%.

Weighting the base case at 50%, the better case at 20% and the worse case at 30% gives an expected return of about +17% over 18 months. The shares have already recovered from 13.2 times earnings in June, so the first and easiest leg of the multiple's reversion is done.

7. What has to be true: three tests, each with a date

1

The winter holds.

Weekly United States flu data should stay firm through December and January. The full-year results on 26-Feb-27 should show fourth-quarter organic growth of 6% to 7% or better and full-year organic growth of at least 3.5%. First-quarter 2027 sales (April 2027) should then grow at a high single-digit rate against a comparison of (3.9)%.
2

Profit grows faster than sales after inflation and currency.

The 2027 guidance on 26-Feb-27 should put organic profit growth at least two points ahead of organic sales growth. The first-half 2027 results (late July 2027) should show the operating margin back above 17%.
3

The new installed base pulls reagents through at a held price.

Each quarter should show SPOTFIRE placements of 700 or more (below 400 is the warning line), SPOTFIRE sales growth of 25% or more, and high single-digit growth in non-respiratory panels once the one-off United States outbreak drops out of the comparison. The 2027 United States Medicare fee schedule for panels tests the price.

#1 Operating environment

Key messageThe environment is improving cyclically, because the respiratory season has turned up, but it is neutral to slightly negative structurally. The next three quarters will flatter the business, and 2028 is the honest test of underlying growth.
11.8% vs 1.9%
US influenza A positivity, week 45, against a year earlier
7.6% vs 0.6%
US laboratory flu positivity, late October, against a year earlier
about 6%
annual growth of the diagnostics market
(7.5)%
organic equipment sales, first half of 2026

Evidence

  • The respiratory cycle has turned up. Influenza A positivity in United States clinical laboratories reached 11.8% in week 45 against 1.9% a year earlier, and the flu peak usually comes in December. Five quarters of low flu prevalence had cut bioMerieux's molecular growth to about 2%
  • Structural demand is intact. Over 80% of revenue is tied to fighting antimicrobial resistance; laboratories short of technicians are automating; single-pathogen tests are still giving way to panels; and the diagnostics market grows about 6% a year
  • Microbiology pricing is firm. Waters raised its net microbiology prices by 1.2 points in the third quarter. China's draft laboratory fee reform lifts microbiology reimbursement by about 10% at the median while cutting molecular tariffs, and microbiology is about 90% of bioMerieux's China business
  • The headwinds are specific. Hospitals are short of capital, so equipment sales fell 7.5% organically in the first half and customers prefer instrument placements, which defer revenue. United States payers increasingly refuse to reimburse large outpatient panels, and Medicare cuts frozen in 2026 could resume in 2027. Japan restricted SPOTFIRE reimbursement in April 2026. Competitors are attacking on several fronts: DiaSorin lets laboratories pay only for the targets they report; Cepheid offers about 15 point-of-care panels; and Waters has launched a faster blood culture system against a bioMerieux franchise worth about 10% of sales. Transport adds just under EUR 1m a month of cost
InferenceThe environment is improving cyclically and is neutral to slightly negative structurally. Management's own cut to the non-respiratory panel growth target, from 10% to 4% to 8%, is the best evidence that the structural pace has slowed.
So whatThe next three quarters flatter the business. 2028 is the honest test of underlying growth, which I put at 4% to 5% a year.
Counter-caseA third mild winter would remove the only strong tailwind, and United States molecular laboratories may be more saturated than the company's targets assume.
What would change my viewFlu data fading before the December peak; a confirmed schedule of Medicare cuts; or final Chinese fee rules that treat microbiology worse than the draft.

Against the marketDeutsche Bank leans on the flu recovery, and Morgan Stanley on competition and China. I think both brokers are right, on different horizons, which is why I sit with consensus on 2027 revenue and a little below it on 2028.

The respiratory tailwind is strong but cyclical, and structural headwinds are present. The operating environment therefore supports step 2 of the argument (the change) for 2027 and leaves it open for 2028.

Score: 58, set by the Rater. The respiratory recovery is a large but cyclical lift to 2027 (US flu positivity 7.6% against 0.6% a year earlier, three quarters of very low comparisons), on structurally intact demand (antimicrobial resistance, laboratory automation, a market growing about 6%) with firm microbiology pricing, but direct external threats (a EUR 35m currency drag in 2026 and 2027, US payer resistance and possible Medicare cuts, Japan's SPOTFIRE restriction, China, Waters and pay-per-target rivals) take one to two points of growth, so beyond 2027 the balance is neutral to slightly negative. Consensus sales growth at the 58th percentile fits a mild net positive concentrated in one year: below Linea Directa's advanced pricing cycle, a touch above OEM's modest recovery.

#2 Corporate change forces

Key messageInternal change is a proven, medium-sized margin force, but in 2026 and 2027 the savings are spent offsetting currency and input inflation, so they will show in reported margins only when those pressures ease.

Evidence

What is working

  • Cost. GO Simple comprises more than fifty initiatives. BIOFIRE pouch automation has risen from about 10% of production lines in late 2024 to about 60%; headcount fell by 200 in the six months to June 2026; procurement saved over EUR 10m and selling and administrative costs fell 2% like-for-like in the first half; and plastics, enzymes and the VITEK MS PRIME instrument have been brought in-house. The constant-currency operating margin rose by about 150 basis points in 2024 and 160 basis points in 2025
  • Discipline. Research projects now need a business case and are cancelled when they fail it; the San Jose site is closed and microbiology research is unified
  • Ownership. Exor's larger stake comes through a reduction of Institut Mérieux's capital, closing in December 2026. A former executive says Exor is already pushing management towards return-on-capital benchmarks
  • Launches. VITEK PRO was cleared in the United States and Europe on 10-Nov-26 and replaces two ageing systems from the first quarter of 2027; the SPOTFIRE vaginitis panel was cleared on 22-Oct-26 with a waiver that allows its use in physician offices

What has gone wrong

  • Sales-force turnover. Merging the BioFire and bioMerieux sales forces in the United States caused heavy turnover, and former staff say almost all of BioFire's legacy marketing team has left
  • A failed platform. The rapid antibiotic susceptibility platform VITEK REVEAL was written down by about EUR 141m to 146m in 2025 (the reports differ)
  • Gaps and losses. SPOTFIRE's test menu is narrow, and Accellix loses money until 2029

InferenceThe cost side of the change rests on strengths the company has demonstrated. The growth side (a broader point-of-care menu, evidence that wins reimbursement, rapid susceptibility testing) rests on strengths the company still has to acquire, and it has already stumbled on one of them.

So what. The self-help is real but invisible for now: reported margins will show it only once currency and input-cost pressures ease, which is why the waterfall below barely rises.
Counter-caseThe Americas are 52% of sales. If the cultural change has damaged commercial execution there, the cost savings are being bought with market share.
What would change my viewEvidence of United States share loss in panels, a further impairment, or SPOTFIRE placements below 400 a quarter.

Against the marketBrokers rank cost savings as the most plausible driver, and I agree. Where I differ is on Exor: asset turnover has fallen from 1.7 to 1.25 times, and an engaged shareholder asking for returns is an under-discussed positive, although my files do not let me size it.

Internal change is a proven, medium-sized margin force with commercial friction attached. It supports step 2 (the change) and explains why step 3 (the route to the financials) runs through the margin later than through sales.

Score: 59, set by the Rater. GO Simple is proven and still delivering (constant-currency margin up about 150bp in 2024 and 160bp in 2025, pouch automation from 10% to 60% of lines, headcount and procurement savings), three launches land in 2027 and Exor's doubled stake brings return-on-capital pressure, but the US sales-force merger has cost talent, VITEK REVEAL was written down by about EUR 141m to 146m, SPOTFIRE's menu is narrow and the ambition has been lowered (the 20% margin target is gone). Real, repair-weighted self-help with commercial friction: a little below Odfjell's acquisition-plus-refinancing, above Shell's incremental savings.

#3 Value chain, business model, financial profile, management

Key messagebioMerieux is a high-quality franchise that under-earns: its moat is real, but heavy research spending, high working capital and controlled governance hold its returns to mid-table. The under-earning explains the discount and is also the opportunity, if capital discipline tightens.

Evidence

  • Industry structure. The four largest diagnostics groups have held about 45% of the market since 2015 and price rationally; specialists such as bioMerieux sit below them. Regulation is a moat: the main respiratory panel now carries Europe's highest-risk certification
  • Position. Value in the diagnostics chain sits in closed-system reagents, where bioMerieux operates. The BIOFIRE installed base of over 27,000 systems is five times Qiagen's, and 51% of BIOFIRE customers run three or more panels. The largest customer is under 1% of sales
  • Weak spots. bioMerieux has a 1% share in immunoassays, where its procalcitonin test is in double-digit decline; its mass spectrometry library is a third the size of Bruker's; and large reference laboratories (22% of the United States market) squeeze its prices
  • Financial profile. Research takes 12.5% of sales, the highest among peers, and working capital is 36% of revenue, so a top-tier gross margin converts into mid-table operating margins and returns. Free cash flow is about 0.9 times net income on FactSet's definition
  • Management and governance. Pierre Boulud (chief executive since July 2023) has a strategy and commercial background and a short record of running profit centres; the finance chief has been in post since 2018. Three of eight non-employee directors are independent. Incentives use absolute targets with no relative shareholder-return test. The chief executive and the finance chief each sold a small holding on 4-Nov-26 after share vestings

Molecular biology is the largest and fastest-growing line in consensus, while immunoassays, the weak spot, shrink.

Inference. bioMerieux is a high-quality franchise that under-earns, and its goals are less stretching than they were: the 20% operating margin target has gone.

So whatThe under-earning explains the valuation discount and is also the opportunity, if capital discipline tightens.

Counter-caseNext-generation sequencing or pay-per-target competitors could turn the closed-system advantage into a price disadvantage over five to ten years.
What would change my viewFalling prices on United States molecular contracts, which the Business Foundations report names as the early warning.

Against the marketMorgan Stanley values the shares at a discount to peers because of competition and China. I think the franchise is intact, and the discount is better explained by weak financial conversion and controlled governance.

The industry structure is favourable and the moat is real, but the financial profile is average and governance is controlled. The franchise supports step 4 (the foundation), with the caveat that its quality does not show fully in returns.

Score: 71, set by the Rater. The structure and moat are strong: closed-system reagents at 91% of sales on five-to-ten-year contracts, over 75% of high-plex syndromic testing, about 40% of clinical microbiology, a BIOFIRE base five times Qiagen's, no customer above 1%, and regulatory barriers; but two parts are ordinary, the financial profile (ROIC 8.8% at the 62nd percentile and operating margin at the 60th, despite a 79th-percentile gross margin, held down by 12.5% research, 36% working capital and 8% capex) and management and governance (a short operating record, a lowered target, 3 of 8 independents), and a fifth of sales swings with the season. With one ordinary part fewer it would match Tenaris; with its stronger moat it edges above Tele2.

#4 Guidance conservatism and the delivery record

Key messageAfter two consecutive cuts, guidance is now conservative and the bar is the lowest since 2023, but management has to re-earn its credibility. A further cut in the next two events is unlikely, and a raise is only modestly likely because management has little reason to hurry.

Evidence on today's guidanceThe 2026 guidance is easy to meet. After nine months of organic growth at 2.7%, the low end of the 2026 range needs fourth-quarter organic growth of only about 4%, and management says the low end assumes respiratory activity as weak as a year ago.

Management is also talking expectations down. It told analysts not to extrapolate the third quarter, expects no China recovery in 2027, and has pre-announced dearer resin and another currency headwind.

Inference. Guidance is conservative on profit but exposed on sales whenever a winter fails. After the July 2026 reset, the bar is the lowest since 2023.

So whatThe probability of a further guidance cut in the next two events is low. The probability of a raise is modest, because management has little reason to hurry.

Counter-caseInvestors said guidance was conservative in November 2025 too. A chief executive who said the company was "exceeding the plan" in February 2026 and then warned in April cannot see the season any better than investors can.
What would change my viewIf the 2027 sales guidance on 26-Feb-27 is set at the top of the 3% to 6% range with the flu tailwind already known, the cushion is thinner than it looks.

Against the marketDeutsche Bank calls management's credibility "challenged", and I agree that it must be re-earned. I think the market underrates the fact that profit guidance held through the 2025 sales cut and broke only once, in April 2026.

Guidance is now conservative, the record is mixed, and estimates have only just stopped falling. The guidance record supports step 3 on the direction of estimate revisions and weakens step 4 (the foundation) on delivery.

Score: 40, set by the Rater. Sales guidance was beaten in 2023 and 2024 but cut in 2025 and again in April 2026, profit guidance held through 2025 but was cut in 2026, the mid-term plan was rebased five months after management said it was being exceeded, and consensus fell 14% in twelve months; current guidance is now conservative (the 2026 low end needs only about 4% in the fourth quarter and assumes a weak season, and management is talking 2027 down). Two consecutive cuts weigh more than the conservative reset, so it sits just below Instalco's single bad year with beats since and above Hexatronic's longer run of walk-backs.

#5 Pricing power, leverage and feedback loops

Key messageOperating leverage is high in both directions, but pricing power covers only half the portfolio and the balance sheet is unused. The gearing explains both the 2026 disappointment and the 2027 recovery, but it does not create a compounding story at the rebased growth rate.

Evidence

  • Pricing power is partial. Microbiology and industrial prices rise about 2% a year, while non-respiratory molecular prices erode about 1.5% a year. In hyperinflation markets, EUR 31m of price increases fully offset currency. Point-of-care customers are price-sensitive
  • Operating leverage is high, in both directions. Operating profit rose 24% on 9.4% organic sales growth in the first half of 2025, and fell 4.9% organically on 0.2% growth a year later. One point of organic growth is worth about EUR 0.13 of EPS
  • Financial leverage is nil. The company has net cash, a 25% payout and borrowing capacity that Deutsche Bank puts at up to EUR 3.5bn. The balance sheet is unused optionality, not leverage
  • Feedback loops run mostly in the company's favour. A larger installed base sells more panels per instrument, and BIOFIRE and SPOTFIRE pouches share production lines in Salt Lake City, so unit costs fall as SPOTFIRE scales. Against that, placed instruments add depreciation and capital spending

Operating leverage cuts both ways: the EBITDA margin rose to 24.4% in the second half of 2025 and fell to 21.6% in the first half of 2026, when revenue fell 3.9%.

InferenceAt 5% organic sales growth, the operating model yields 7% to 8% organic profit growth, and less after currency and inflation. Profit growth is outsized only when respiratory volume surges.

So what. The gearing explains both the 2026 disappointment and the 2027 recovery, but it does not create a compounding story at the rebased growth rate.
Counter-caseSPOTFIRE may cannibalise BIOFIRE at a lower price per test, turning a volume gain into a margin loss.
What would change my viewTwo consecutive halves of organic profit growth three or more points ahead of organic sales growth would show leverage outrunning the drags.

Against the marketConsensus has EPS growth of 9.5% in 2028, which assumes the leverage comes through cleanly. I forecast 7%.

Operating leverage is real and the installed-base feedback loop is growing, but pricing power covers only half the portfolio and there is no financial leverage. This topic supports step 3 (the route to the financials) for 2027 and weakens any claim of outsized earnings growth beyond 2027.

Score: 65, set by the Rater. Operating leverage is high and proven in both directions (operating profit +24% on 9.4% organic growth, then (4.9)% on 0.2%; about 60% drop-through, two points of volume worth about 6% of EPS), with an installed-base loop (more panels per instrument, shared BIOFIRE and SPOTFIRE lines) and proven cost-out scope; but pricing power covers only about half the portfolio (microbiology +2% a year, molecular (1.5)%), financial leverage is nil and currency and input costs absorb the gearing at the rebased growth rate. The forecast ratio of EPS to revenue growth (about 6.4% against 4.8%, about 1.3 times against a Universe median of about 2) understates the structure, so the score sits above 50 but below the 75 band, which needs pricing as a second proven gear.

Reading the forecasts

  • Double-digit growth is not in the base case. Revenue growth looks strong only in the first half of 2027 (about 8%), because the comparison is weak; the second half slows to about 3.5% against a strong comparison
  • Growth and margins are lower than in the past, not higher. Revenue grew about 7% a year from 2019 to 2025, and adjusted EPS rose 9% in 2025 on the company's like-for-like basis; I forecast revenue growth under 5% and EPS growth of about 6%. The EBITDA margin regains its 2025 level only in 2028
  • The company's delivery record makes the base case plausible. The base case uses only what the business has already shown: a sticky installed base, mid-single-digit growth outside respiratory testing, and cost control. The upside needs strengths the company has not yet shown
  • The range of outcomes is wide and its skew changes over time. Brokers' bear and bull cases for 2027 EPS run from 4.10 to 5.42, about (14)% to +13% around my figure. The skew is upward into mid-2027 (low comparisons, a live flu season) and downward after it (tough comparisons, resin costs, Medicare)

Revenue grew from EUR 2.7bn to 4.1bn between 2019 and 2025, but the EBITDA margin has not returned to its 2021 peak.

Counter-caseMy 2026 forecast needs the second half of 2026 to deliver revenue growth of about 9% and an operating margin above 18%, so I may be extrapolating one good quarter.
What would change my viewFourth-quarter organic growth below 5% would take my 2026 and 2027 forecasts below consensus.

Against the marketI agree with consensus to 2027. I am below consensus in 2028 because I let currency and input costs absorb more of the savings.

I forecast mid-single-digit revenue growth and 6% to 7% EPS growth, with no double-digit year. The forecasts weaken step 3 on the size of the earnings response, while supporting its timing.

#7 Scope for upgrades not yet in guidance or consensus

Key messageThe scope for upgrades is modest in the numbers, larger in the narrative and in analysts' ratings, and concentrated in the next two events. It is the thinnest link in the argument.

What is left after what is already counted

2026Consensus implies fourth-quarter organic growth of about 6%. Flu data for weeks 44 and 45, published on 16 and 23 November after most estimates were set (3 to 6 November), support about 7%. The difference is worth EUR 10m to 15m of sales and under 1% of EPS
2027I cannot name evidence that the sell-side lacks, so my forecast is at consensus. The real scope is in timing: a strong first half could pull estimates up 1% to 4% before the second half tests them
2028 and beyondThe scope is flat to negative. Management's microbiology growth target of 3% to 5% looks beatable if China's fee reform helps, but resumed Medicare cuts and the price of the vaginitis panel (which consensus assumes is monetised quickly, while management calls its price uncertain) are risks, not upside
Unpriced optionalityDeploying the balance sheet is in nobody's numbers, and my files do not let me judge its likelihood

Guidance is more likely to be met than raised, while 2027 consensus EPS leans towards upgrades over the next two events.

The scope for upgrades is modest in numbers, larger in narrative and ratings, and concentrated in the next two events. It supports step 3 (the route to the financials) only partly, and it is the thinnest link in the argument.

#9 Riskiness and simplicity

Key messageThe case is simple to follow and moderately risky: it has one large, exogenous but visible risk (the respiratory season) and several slow structural ones. The franchise and the balance sheet bound the downside, and cyclicality caps the upside.

Three drivers explain most of the earnings.

Driver 1

The respiratory season

Driver 2

The operating margin

Driver 3

The euro

Evidence

  • Simplicity. Three drivers explain most of the earnings: the respiratory season, the operating margin and the euro. The balance sheet adds no risk
  • Fragility. The case needs a normal winter, which nobody controls and which failed in each of the last two years; it needs payers not to cut panel reimbursement; and it needs currency to cost no more than guided
  • Suddenness and trackability. Disappointments land on quarterly sales releases: the April 2026 guidance cut took the shares from about EUR 91 to 71 within the month. The main driver is unusually trackable, through weekly public flu data; reimbursement and China are not
  • Materiality. Morgan Stanley's bear case is EUR 57 a share (13 times EPS of 4.36). On 4-Nov-26, options implied a 6% chance of the shares trading below EUR 57 within a year, a 19% chance below EUR 75 and a 35% chance above EUR 106
  • Sector precedents. The multiple fell from 41.7 times in May 2020 to 13.2 times in June 2026 as pandemic testing normalised. DiaSorin's sales fell 15.6% in 2023, Qiagen warned in April 2026, and Sysmex's China sales fell 24%. Diagnostics stocks de-rate hard when growth is rebased
  • Environment. Viewforth's weekly tilts are Overweight for the sector, Neutral for healthcare and Double Underweight for France on the sovereign premium. With 94% of sales outside France, the French tilt is a listing risk, not an earnings one. A EUR 10.8bn company with net cash passes the Fragility test. The earnings do not need a lower discount rate, but a lower discount rate would help the re-rating
Counter-caseA trackable risk is not a predictable one: the strength of the season is known only weeks ahead, after positions are set.
What would change my viewRespiratory testing falling below a fifth of sales as the menu broadens would lower the risk, but nothing in my files suggests that within two years.

Against the marketOptions pricing and the Risks report both rate a severe fall as unlikely. I agree, and I put a 30% probability on a moderate fall.

The risk is moderate and simple to follow, with a sudden but observable main hazard. Riskiness shapes step 6 (the reward and the skew): the franchise and the balance sheet bound the downside, and cyclicality caps the upside.

Score: 52, set by the Rater. The case is simple (season, margin, euro) with net cash, and its main driver is trackable weekly, but the 2027 EPS cone runs about (14)% to +13%, the season is exogenous, failed in the last two winters and lands suddenly on quarterly sales releases (April 2026 took the shares from about 91 to 71), reimbursement and China are slow and opaque, and diagnostics de-rates hard when growth is rebased; options price only a 6% chance of a fall below EUR 57. A moderate, exogenous range with no balance-sheet amplification: just below NKT's backlog visibility, just above IMCD's leverage-plus-FX.

#10 Lifecycle phase

Key messageThe stock is turning up, early and unconfirmed. The dashboard's rule still places it in Stalling, but that label lags because it weighs twelve months of estimate cuts that ended with the July reset.

The evidence leans towards an early turn up, with the dashboard's Stalling label lagging.

Against Stalling

The share price is 39% above its low; the multiple has risen from 13.2 to 17.9 times; estimates have risen over one and three months after a year of cuts; and a quarter has been beaten and guidance held.

For Stalling

Guidance has not been raised, four analysts in five do not rate the shares a buy, and the long-term trend line is not rising.

InferenceThe evidence against Stalling is more recent than the evidence for it, so I read the stock as turning up, early.

So what. The first leg of the recovery (relief) is done. A second leg needs the thesis to broaden from "the flu is back" to "the rebased targets are being beaten".
Counter-caseA soft fourth quarter or first quarter would make the turn a failed one and return the stock to Stalling.
What would change my viewA guidance raise, or two quarters of profit growth ahead of sales growth, would move the stock to the thesis-broadening phase.

Against the marketDeutsche Bank's view that "the earnings inflection is here" is the same reading as mine; Morgan Stanley's reading is Stalling. I side with Deutsche Bank on direction and with Morgan Stanley on how far the turn goes.

The stock is turning up, early and unconfirmed. The lifecycle phase supports step 5 (the setup), and explains why momentum is the setup's missing element.

Score: 60, set by the Rater. I side with the memo's early Turning Up over the computed Stalling: a beaten quarter (8.1% organic), guidance held, estimates up over one and three months after a year of cuts and the multiple off its 13.2x low; but the turn is unconfirmed (no raise, four in five analysts not Buy, a flat 200-day average), the first relief leg is already in the price, and a soft fourth or first quarter would make it a failed turn. That places it just below Nexans's paused Reinforcing and above Greggs's Bottoming/early Turning.

#11 The fair multiple

Key messageA fair multiple of about 19.5 times two-year forward earnings is more realistic than the 23.0 times guideline, so most of the headline return depends on which multiple proves right.

The guidelineThe guideline fair multiple is 23.0 times two-year forward earnings, the 40th percentile of the stock's ten-year history, set for the Stalling phase and 29% above today's multiple. I do not have the guideline's figure for a turning-up phase.

My view: 23 times is a generous 18-month destination, for four reasons

  • The ten-year history is flattered. It includes 2017 to 2021, when the shares traded at 25 to 40 times earnings on double-digit growth and pandemic testing
  • Recent history is lower. The shares have not closed a month above 23 times since December 2022. The last approach (22.9 times in July 2025) came when the market still believed in 7% growth and a 20% margin. The five-year interquartile range is 19.5 to 22.6 times, and the two-year median is 19.6 times
  • Growth no longer supports 23 times. With EPS growing 6% to 7% a year, 23 times is more than three times the growth rate
  • Reference points are lower. DiaSorin trades at 16.4 times, and brokers use 15 times (Morgan Stanley) to 20 times (Deutsche Bank)
So what. I would expect a multiple of 19 to 20 times if the rebased targets are delivered. The guideline is reachable only if the market again believes in double-digit earnings growth, which needs a strength the company has not shown since the reset.
Counter-caseQuality franchises at trough multiples often overshoot on the way back, and a defensive bid for healthcare could carry the multiple further than growth alone justifies.
What would change my viewA raised mid-term target or a visible use of the balance sheet.

Against the marketThe market's multiple of 17.9 times is below my range of 19 to 20 times, and the guideline of 23.0 times is above it.

My fair multiple is about 19.5 times, against a guideline of 23.0 times. The fair multiple bears directly on step 6 (the reward and the skew): most of the headline return depends on which multiple is right.

Score: 76, set by the Rater. Cheap on one and neutral on the other gives B; placed at the floor because much of the cheapness is deserved: the ten-year range includes the 25x-40x of 2017-2021 and pandemic testing, the growth target has been permanently lowered, and on the memo's own fair multiple of about 19.5x (the five-year interquartile floor) the rerating left is only about 9%.

#13 Summary conclusion

bioMerieux is a high-quality reagent franchise at a first-quartile multiple, with the cause of its de-rating clearing and three quarters of easy comparisons ahead. The earnings engine behind it is modest (6% to 7% EPS growth a year), the mid-term bar has been lowered for good, and the first leg of the recovery is already in the price. The case is real, moderately strong and moderately sure: it is a reversion with a soft growth engine, not an earnings step-up. Evidence of profit growing clearly ahead of sales after currency and inflation, or a use of the balance sheet, would make the case stronger.

What to watch, in order

The case is tested in six steps from December 2026 to November 2027, with the heaviest evidence on 26-Feb-27 and in April 2027.

Dec 2026 to Jan 20271. Weekly United States flu data through the December peak and into January
26-Feb-272. Fourth-quarter organic growth, the 2026 operating margin and, above all, the shape of the 2027 guidance (the gap between profit growth and sales growth, and the currency and resin assumptions)
April 20273. First-quarter sales against the (3.9)% comparison; SPOTFIRE placements and reagent growth
2027, undated4. The 2027 United States Medicare fee schedule for panels and the final Chinese laboratory fee rules
Late July 20275. The first-half operating margin and whether guidance is raised
November 20276. Third-quarter sales against the toughest comparison, and the start of the 2027/28 respiratory season

Thesis's Change Forces' Strength: 57, set by the Rater. Mild positive input forces (a large but one-year cyclical tailwind netted by structural headwinds, topic 1 at 58, and proven but repair-weighted self-help with commercial friction, topic 2 at 59) reach profits only as about 6.4% EPS growth (topic 6 at 54), below the Universe median of about 11%, so the net change is real but modest and front-loaded, a mild net positive in the high 50s.

Foundations' Robustness: 72, set by the Rater. A near-locked recurring reagent franchise with dominant shares, non-discretionary hospital demand and net cash (topic 3 at 71) is robust, but the dented delivery record (topic 4 at 40), average returns and family-controlled governance, plus a fifth of sales that swings with the season, keep it below the stability-carried 75 band and well above the ordinary-structure 60s.

Setups' Fit/Crispness: 63, set by the Rater. The case fits 'CfC Clearing in HQ low-cyclicality business on Q1/Q2 multiple' on quality, a first-quartile multiple and a clearing cause for concern, but two elements of the setup's mechanism are loose in substance: the business is not low-cyclicality (a fifth of sales swings with epidemiology) and the normal it reverts to has been reset lower, so it sits below the 75 for a quality business at a trough with its concern clearing; weak momentum is timing and is not counted here.

Case Riskiness: 55, set by the Rater. Few, visible drivers, net cash, a multiple low in its own range and now-conservative guidance constrain the risk (topic 9 at 52), but the main driver is an uncontrollable winter that has forced guidance cuts two years running and moves the shares by a fifth when it fails, so the risk is more than paper cuts and the case sits a little above the middle.

In the Rater's notes, "CfC Clearing in HQ low-cyclicality business on Q1/Q2 multiple" means a cause for concern clearing in a high-quality, low-cyclicality business on a first- or second-quartile multiple.

End notes

1. Sources. The Latest Earnings Review is dated 24-Nov-26 and covers the first-half 2026 results (six months to 30-Jun-26, published 28-Jul-26) and the third-quarter sales release of 3-Nov-26. FactSet's last reported period is also June 2026, so no results have been reported after it; the next results are due on 26-Feb-27. The standard research reports are Change Forces (24-Nov-26), Business Foundations (20-Jul-26; it pre-dates the half-year results and the target reset), Leadership Foundations (24-Nov-26) and Risks (24-Nov-26).

2. Dates and inputs not in my files. The exact date of the first-quarter 2027 sales release (April 2027) is not in my files. The 2026 SPOTFIRE sales base of about EUR 230m is my inference from the company's statement that its 25% to 40% growth target "implies about EUR 400m" in 2028.

3. Net debt. The Change Forces report gives end-2025 net debt of EUR 211m, while FactSet and the Business Foundations report show net cash of EUR 108m; I use net cash of EUR 108m, which is also the starting point of the Financial Analyst's model (EUR 108.4m at 31-Dec-25).

4. Bases of the 2025 figures, and the model against the Analyst. The Analyst's forecast table uses the brokers' basis: the company's contributive operating income before non-recurring items (EUR 728m for 2025), the brokers' EBITDA margin (24.5% for 2025) and the company's adjusted diluted EPS (EUR 4.64 for 2025). The Financial Analyst's model confirms each of these figures on that basis. The model's own table shows 2025 on FactSet's basis, after amortisation of acquired intangibles: EBITA of EUR 654.7m, an EBITDA margin of 23.9% and EPS of 4.58. The model reproduces the Analyst's EPS forecasts to within EUR 0.03 in every year; its 2026 free cash flow is EUR 455.1m against the Analyst's EUR 505m. The model does not include minority interests or hybrid bond coupons, and it has no bear or bull cases.

5. The model's return split. The split is on the return's own basis: the two-year-forward price-to-earnings multiple and two-year-forward earnings per share, today against each horizon. The multiple and earnings parts multiply (one plus the first, times one plus the second, less one, is the change in the share price), and dividends add to that. The template's own split (TSR Dupont sheet, rows 46 and 47) measures the same return on trailing twelve-month earnings and the trailing multiple: at the 18-month column, +11.1% from the multiple and +24.9% from earnings; at the three-year column, +9.3% from the multiple and +38.1% from earnings. That split reads differently when earnings over the next twelve months are flat or falling, so use the split shown in the chart. The two horizons are the model's fixed columns after the last reported period, so they end on the dates shown (31-Dec-27 and 30-Jun-29), not 18 months and three years from today. The model's multiple today (18.2 times) differs from the memo's 17.9 times because the model uses the share price of 21-Nov-26.

6. Charts. Charts drawn for this page take their figures from the memo; where the memo gives only totals, the balance is shown and labelled as such.

Figures corrected

None.
